svg.text: Bundle invariant: fleetd writes the bundles row and its bundle_members rows in 1 transaction before the bundle_build job (A27).
Bundle invariant: A bundle moves the feature ref only by compare-and-set from its base tip; a failed compare-and-set drops the bundle and its members go back to ready (I9, A34).
Bundle invariant: A task branch is a member of at most 1 bundle that is not ended (I12).

Bundle invariant: fleetd deletes the candidate ref refs/horch/bundle/<id> of a landed, failed or dropped bundle when no child bundle of it is building, gating or passed, and reads the ref store again to
verify the deletion (A34).
Bundle invariant: The fast gate runs once on a bundle, as a fast_gate job keyed by the candidate tip and the base tip (A23, A33).
Feature invariant: I8: a feature is merged only when its changes are in the primary branch by content, also after a squash merge.

Feature invariant: I9: a feature branch moves only by fast-forward to a candidate that passed its gate; each ref move is a compare-and-set on seen_tip or seen_remote_tip, and a failed compare-and-set moves
nothing and records the new tip.
Feature invariant: I10: before each rebase or forced update of a branch, a rescue ref of the old tip exists.
Feature invariant: A feature is ready only with a full gate pass on its current tip over the fetched tip of the primary branch, and each idea of the feature integrating, cancelled or parked.
Feature invariant: A gate pass goes stale when either judged tip moves (04 F5).
Feature invariant: A feature is stacked on at most 1 older feature.
Feature invariant: A feature has 1 of 4 states, open, ready, merged and abandoned; merged and abandoned are terminal, and only the operator sets abandoned (A28, A34).
Feature invariant: fleetd does not queue a rebase of a feature branch while 1 of its bundles is in gating or in passed (A34).
Feature invariant: A merge with ideas in flight moves those ideas to a new feature (A28, A34).
Feature invariant: With remote = none, fleetd does not fetch, push or open a pull request; the pull request state follows the feature state (A28).
Feature invariant: A failed push sets push_state failed and push_not_before; at 3 failures in a row, 1 item goes on the needs-you list (A33).
TaskBranch invariant: I8: a task branch is landed only when its changes are in the feature branch by content.
TaskBranch invariant: I11: every fleet branch in git has a branches row; one without is adopted as an orphan row, never deleted.
TaskBranch invariant: I12: a branch is deleted only when landed, merged or rescued, and no git stash entry names it; a task branch is a member of at most 1 bundle that is not ended.
TaskBranch invariant: A task branch is ready only when its task is done (verified).
TaskBranch invariant: Under the land lock, just before the fast-forward, the task is still landing and held by its worker (04 F9).
TaskBranch invariant: A red land after a rebase resets the branch to its tip from before the land (04 F7).
TaskBranch invariant: An escalated task branch is abandoned only by the operator and only after worktree-rescued (connect N4).
TaskBranch invariant: conflicted and gate_failed are owned by fleetd; a failed resolver or fix attempt adds 1 to repair_attempts, and at max_attempts the branch goes on the needs-you list (A27, A34).
TaskBranch invariant: A branch of a cancelled task is abandoned only after its rescue ref is written (A34, connect F10).

Port IntegrationCommands (driving) via ReconcilePassDriver (fleet-runtime) and CommandChannelHandler: one operation per use case; called by the reconcile pass and the command channel (abandon-task-branch,
abandon-feature: operator requests with request_id and the operator token).
Port IntegrationQueries (driving): read models WorktreeList (branch side), PullRequestView, TrialMergeResult.
Port IntegrationEventHandlers (driving) via InProcessReconcileConsumer: policies on task-done, task-escalated, task-cancelled, attempt-failed (repair_attempts), worktree-rescued, assumptions-written,
direct-idea-accepted, idea-tasks-landed, pull-request-closed, and job-abandoned and job-requeued of its own job kinds.

Port GitObserver (driving) via GitPollObserver: primary-branch-moved, remote-tips-fetched and check-merged facts read from git and from remote_tips each pass (clock initiated), and pull-request-merged and
pull-request-closed from GitHub.
Port FeatureRepository (driven) via SqliteFeatureRepository: load and save Feature with GateRuns and TrialMerges.
Port TaskBranchRepository (driven) via SqliteTaskBranchRepository: load and save TaskBranch by name.
Port EventPublisher (driven) via LedgerEventLog: writes the event row in the same ledger transaction.

Port GitGateway (driven) via CliGitGateway (vcs::git, vcs::network, vcs::landing): the only caller of rebase, merge-tree, fast-forward, push, fetch and branch delete (define N5); content containment, stash

list; a git command that reads or writes a working tree or uses the network runs as a job through the JobQueue of fleet-runtime; only git update-ref on a local ref, a compare-and-set, runs in part 3 of a pass

Port GateRunner (driven) via ProjectGateRunner: queues the declared fast gate and full gate of the project as fast_gate and full_gate jobs on a candidate tip, and reads their results in a later pass (A23).

Port PullRequestGateway (driven) via GhCliPullRequests: open-pull-request: opens a pull request with pr gh, or pushes and builds the compare URL with pr manual; marks it a draft when the feature goes back to
open; nothing with remote = none (A28).
Port LandLock (driven) via LedgerLandLock: the land lock (1 h, 5 tries).
Port Clock (driven) via LedgerFleetClock: due_at of branch rows and gate staleness.
Port RescueRefGateway (driven) via InProcessWorktreeCustody: asks worktree-custody to write and read back a rescue ref of the old tip before each rebase or forced update (I10, A13).
Port BundleRepository (driven) via SqliteBundleRepository: load and save Bundle with its BundleMembers (bundles, bundle_members) and the candidate ref of each bundle.
